This is regarding the Handitran service side of the app only

It’s been well over a year since we’ve used this service, and it was called Via then, so this is the first time under the new title (new company as well?) of Arlington Transportation.

Scheduling rides is very easy and straightforward, even though it usually has to be done at least a day or two in advance. But for Handitran service that is expected and generally not a problem.

We were given a 30 minute window for when the driver will be picking us up, which is just fine. 

If they had just stopped there, this would be a five star rating. But no… 

Someone decided to add real-time driver tracking on a map, just like all the other driving apps, and whoever decided to do that didn’t know what they were doing!

When we looked at the driver tracking, it showed him arriving at the far end of that 30-minute pick up window, so we were taking our time. Then the doorbell rang! You guessed it! It was the Handitran driver! 

As we are standing there talking, I get a notification from the app that said our driver was 30 minutes away!

The driver explained that you simply cannot trust the map tracking in the app, or it’s notifications, and just be ready by the beginning of the half hour window we were given. 

Good to know!

No other driving or delivery app, not even the old Via app, has had this problem for us for Years & Years! Only the Arlington Transportation app! They stand alone in not getting this foundational functionality of the entire thing done, in all this time. They need to simply remove that part of the app!

Meanwhile, ignore it and be ready by the pick up window time, and you’ll be fine

I've lived in Twin Falls for 18 years as of this October, and especially in the last few of those years, it's definitely needed some form of public transportation. I much prefer this over a traditional bus system simply because it's much easier to plan my day around. The app is easy to use, which is good for totally blind users like myself. The only slight problem is that parts of it don't work quite as well for screen reading software, for instance you can't edit what you've written in the destination and pick up fields if you make a mistake, unless of course you either can count how many spaces back that mistake was or you delete everything and start over. Aside from that, the app is excellent and seems to be very accurate. It tells you how much you can expect to pay for your ride and how long they estimate your weight will be. Then, when somebody has been assigned to pick you up and tells you who they are and roughly when they expect to be at your destination. Once you have a driver you get two notifications, well, technically three. You get the initial notification of who your driver is, then once they're a few blocks away you get a notification saying that they're arriving soon, plus a final notification when they arrive. Unfortunately, another issue as far as blindness accessibility goes is that from my experimentation it's impossible to rate your driver, or at least extremely difficult. This is kind of sad because so far, and admittedly I've only use the service twice, but my experiences have been positive, so of course I would want to give my drivers positive ratings. Unfortunately, that part of the app does not appear to be accessible.

TL;DR: Buy a car, get a cab, or walk. So for a bit of background information, my usual bus ride from the terminal takes about 15 minutes on Sault College, bringing me up to the corner of Northern and Pine. Tonight was my first time using the service, and it seriously left something to be desired. At 7:15, when the service started, there were 5 buses at the terminal ready to go, and a few passengers and myself were put on one of them. With 5 different buses, I thought that we were all sorted based on general area of destination, and the app showed a 30 minute bus ride, which was already a bit longer than I was expecting. Somehow, the system decided that the best route for our passengers was to go all the way to the west end, all the way to the east end, then finally all the way up to my stop, by Sault College. The timing of the route went as follows: 45 minutes doing laps in the west end, followed by a detour lap around the terminal, followed by a 20 minute trip out and around the east end, and finally a 10 minute route to "my stop". My stop turned out to be about 4 "bus stop" signs away from my normal sign, and I walked the rest of the way. The bus then drove all the way up past my usual stop and kept going. So when all was said and done, what would normally have been a 15 minute bus ride and a 5 minute walk turned into an hour and 15 minute lap of the city and a 20 minute walk. Sault On Demand is a service that is designed to save the city money, and in doing so is driving more and more people away from the transit system and towards taking a cab. The app does what it says it does, but the service behind the app needs a lot of work and maybe even an hour of testing before it should even consider going public.

Picturesque Travel Experience. Dearest Gentle Reader,

One must question an experience as grand as the Stevens Shuttle. 

Could something so divine even manifest in a reality as tarnished as our own?

Today my expectations were not only blown away but elevated beyond the point once thought possible. My travel experience this night, the thirty-first of August in the year two thousand and twenty four, anno domini, was truly magnificent. As I ambled out into the cold, unfeeling streets of Hoboken, New Jersey, surrounded by numerous ne’er-do-wells, I was met by the warm, angelic light emanating from a solitary black van.

Our eyes interlocked in the soft glisten of the rearview mirror. His clandestine gaze offered me bodily comfort on this humid summer night.
As we traversed the softly lit avenues of this here township, I was whisked into a etherial realm of ecstasy and wonder. My singular reproach twas that his grizzled visage could not face me at all times. None the less I was enraptured.

The colossal waves of sorrow that washed over my body as I was forced to depart from his presence, have resided within my soul ever since. Without him, the road laid ‘fore me resembled only the damned expanse of Tartarus. However, I hold comfort in the words he bestowed upon me-self. A soft response to a cracked goodbye … “You too”.

Wherefore am I, a mere mortal being, worthy of the presence of such a pillar of the modern world.

-J.H. Cromwell

Driver safety. As a driver, I feel like Gozone does not take driver safety or driver support seriously enough. Many passengers claim they are using a pass as payment, but most of the time they either don’t have one or try to avoid paying properly. Drivers are often put in uncomfortable situations dealing with homeless individuals, passengers with dogs, school students misusing accounts, and people showing bad behavior.

There are times when, out of fear for my own safety, I still give rides because you never know how someone might react over a $1.50 fare. I don’t want drivers to feel unsafe or pressured just to avoid conflict. Another issue is adults using kids’ accounts to pay only $0.75 for rides, which is unfair and easily abused.

Gozone also does a poor job educating passengers on how the service actually works. Many people think it operates like Uber or Lyft, when in reality it is a corner-to-corner pickup and drop-off service. Even after explaining this politely to passengers multiple times, some still call drivers arrogantly demanding pickup directly from their house or office.

On top of that, even after driving long shifts — sometimes up to 10 hours — drivers don’t receive proper paid breaks or enough support. The company really needs stricter verification, better rider education, stronger rider accountability, fair treatment for drivers, and more focus on driver safety.
